recognize_zh: 紅色箭頭所指的多染性（偏藍）紅血球內，可見沿細胞邊緣彎繞的紫色細線環（Cabot ring）；藍色箭頭指向同一細胞邊緣的深色小圓點，為 Howell-Jolly 小體。
features: Polychromatic, slightly bluish red cell containing a thin violet curved ring inclusion along its periphery (red arrow)
Small, dense, dark round inclusion at the cell margin consistent with a Howell-Jolly body (blue arrow)
Small central clear area within the same cell
Surrounding red cells show anisocytosis and mild poikilocytosis with irregular contours
No leukocytes or parasites in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with anisocytosis and mild poikilocytosis. A polychromatic red cell contains a thin, curved, violet-staining ring-like thread tracing its periphery, consistent with a Cabot ring, and a small dense round basophilic inclusion at its edge consistent with a Howell-Jolly body. No intraerythrocytic parasites are identified. Findings are consistent with a Cabot ring and Howell-Jolly body, reflecting stressed erythropoiesis in hemolytic anemia.

ddx.vs: A falciparum ring is a delicate blue loop with one or two red chromatin dots often in normal-colored cells, whereas a Cabot ring is a violet thread hugging the membrane and the Howell-Jolly body is a separate, larger dense dot.
Pappenheimer bodies are multiple fine peripheral granules that stain with Prussian blue, unlike this single round Howell-Jolly body.
Basophilic stippling consists of numerous fine or coarse granules dispersed throughout the cell rather than a single thread and a single dot.
